title: Single-Query Prediction with Tumor2Line
text: Tumor2Line matches query population candidate cancer cell lines using transcriptomic similarity population level. Query samples may represent patient tumors, PDOs, PDXs, organoids, tumor-derived models. Overview Tumor2Line standard Tumor2Line workflow constructs shared molecular representation using scaled PCA performs population-aware matching unbalanced optimal transport (uOT). many practical applications, however, user may already established reference query cohort later receive single new query sample. Tumor2Line therefore supports two conceptually different single-query prediction strategies: Population mode: project new query frozen reference molecular space, add reference query population, rerun population-aware uOT matching; Transfer mode: project new query reference molecular space, identify similar reference queries, transfer existing Tumor2Line cell-line rankings new query. Population mode retains full population-aware matching framework recommended strategy reference query cohort available. Transfer mode provides faster approximate prediction strategy uses k = 5 similar reference queries default. tutorial uses bundled PDMR-format example dataset. One PDMR tumor held treated newly arriving query sample. remaining tumors form reference query cohort. known PDMR pairing information retained final evaluation used construct either prediction.

code: summarize_heldout_prediction <- function(prediction, true_cellline_ids, mode) {    ranking <- prediction$ranking    true_rows <- ranking[     ranking$CellLine_ID %in% true_cellline_ids, , drop = FALSE]    if (nrow(true_rows) == 0) {     return(       data.frame(         Mode = mode,         Top_candidate = NA_character_,         True_CellLine_ID = NA_character_,         True_pair_rank = NA_integer_,         Top1 = FALSE,         Top3 = FALSE,         Reciprocal_rank = NA_real_,         stringsAsFactors = FALSE))   }    true_row <- true_rows[which.min(true_rows$rank), , drop = FALSE]   top_row <- ranking[ranking$rank == 1L, , drop = FALSE]    data.frame(     Mode = mode,     Top_candidate = top_row$CellLine_ID[1],     True_CellLine_ID = true_row$CellLine_ID[1],     True_pair_rank = as.integer(true_row$rank[1]),     Top1 = true_row$rank[1] <= 1,     Top3 = true_row$rank[1] <= 3,     Reciprocal_rank = 1 / true_row$rank[1],     stringsAsFactors = FALSE   ) } population_evaluation <- summarize_heldout_prediction(   population_prediction,   true_cellline_ids,   "Population" )  transfer_evaluation <- summarize_heldout_prediction(   transfer_prediction,   true_cellline_ids,   "Transfer" )  single_query_evaluation <- rbind(   population_evaluation,   transfer_evaluation )  single_query_evaluation #>         Mode         Top_candidate      True_CellLine_ID True_pair_rank  Top1 #> 1 Population 435261__313_R__J1_PDC 435261__313_R__J1_PDC              1  TRUE #> 2   Transfer 381356__305_R__J1_PDC 435261__313_R__J1_PDC              4 FALSE #>    Top3 Reciprocal_rank #> 1  TRUE            1.00 #> 2 FALSE            0.25

text: Generalized core API tumor-first population query population, allowing tumors, PDOs, PDXs, organoids, tumor-derived samples. Made known pairing information optional (pair_col = NULL default); pairs used evaluation. Added SampleRole (query/cellline) independently biological SampleType. Renamed algorithm-facing identifiers Tumor_ID Query_ID rho_tumor rho_query. Changed max_pcs NULL default retained PC number determined cumulative PCA variance threshold unless user explicitly supplies upper limit.
